text:
olivia: FYI seeing a 30-40% throughput drop on prod-gpu-pool-usw2 starting ~11:23 UTC, lots of worker restarts and intermittent latency spikes. First flagging here so we can coordinate.

sasha: which commit/rollout was active at ~11:20? any recent kernel changes?

olivia: rollout 2026-03-18T11:15: config tweak: kernel-selection: prefer_fast=true, batching.window_ms lowered from 30->15. No infra deploys.

ram: logs show repeated OOM on GPU0 then quick worker restart loop, then host-level allocator fragmentation. snippet from worker:```
[2026-03-18T11:23:41Z] ERROR oom: GPU 0 OOM, requested 124.5MB, available 98.2MB
[2026-03-18T11:23:41Z] WARN restarting worker pid=4221 kernel=fallback_quant
```

maya: also seeing a sharp increase in KV-cache evictions around same time. eviction rate went from ~2/s to ~45/s. KV hits drop -> more prefix recomputation -> higher memory pressure.

infra-oncall: @olivia @sasha rolling a temporary mitigation: disable prefer_fast kernel routing and set batching.window_ms back to 30ms on the affected pool. I'll start a staged config change to avoid mass restarts. :wrench:

sergio: quick profiling result from perf agent (small sample): kernel chooser switched to a lower-memory kernel but it had worse streaming behavior leading to small allocations churn. CPU stacks point to continuous kernel selection fallback code path.

olivia: timeline looks like: batching window shrink -> more smaller batches -> KV shared caches less effective (lower prefix reuse) -> more allocations -> allocator slabs fragmented -> per-GPU available blocks decreased -> OOMs and restarts.

ram: agree. patch in runtime changed `prefer_fast=true` introduced a path that avoids pre-reserved KV buffers for small-batch scenarios. That reduced tail latency for some traces but increased alloc churn. Possibly a regression.

sasha: can we replay a failing trace locally? @ram do you have the seed/trace id?

ram: trace id: trace-20260318-112324-qd7. Uploading a minimal repro to /mnt/perf/repro/trace-qd7.tar.gz. It reproduces OOM on a single 16GB test GPU with the new kernel routing.

infra-oncall: mitigation applied to 3/4 hosts in pool at 11:31 UTC: revert kernel routing + batching window rollback. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: config-change: revert prefer_fast on pool prod-gpu-pool-usw2 by infra-oncall at 2026-03-18T11:31:02Z :white_check_mark:

maya: after rollback eviction rate fell back to ~3/s and throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline by 11:42. No further restarts.

olivia: action items: 1) ram to open a perf-regression PR that reintroduces pre-reserved KV buffer for small-batches and add unit tests for allocator usage; 2) sasha to add a perf test for kernel-selection under small-batch workload; 3) infra to add a short-circuit in autoscaler to avoid simultaneous restarts on pool-wide config churn.

ram: will open PR with diffs and perf numbers, include microbench for 8-32 token sequences.

sasha: I'll sketch the test harness and add it to the nightly perf matrix.

infra-oncall: noted for autoscaler change. Also adding a dashboard panel for KV eviction rate and kernel-fallback count per-host.

sergio: one more: add a regression alert that fires when throughput drops >20% AND OOMs > 5 across pool in 5m. Saves manual triage next time.

olivia: thanks everyone. marking incident as mitigated for now, will keep thread open for PR links and follow-ups. :thumbsup:

ram: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812 - includes benchmarks and allocator fix.

sasha: added perf job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/kernel-selection-small-batch.queued

infra-oncall: leaving config revert in place until PR is validated. Will coordinate gradual roll forward after validation.

olivia: closing loop: summary for ops log -> throughput drop caused by regression in kernel-routing that removed a pre-reserved KV buffer optimization for small-batch workloads, leading to high eviction rates, allocator slab fragmentation, GPU OOMs and worker restarts. Mitigation: revert routing & batching window rollback. Next: PR+tests and autoscaler guard.

deploy-bot: incident-note: incident_id=INC-2026-03-18-1802556789; severity=medium; status=mitigated
